title: The Question That Learned to Ask Itself

features.name: the-asking-mirror
features.desc-on-touch: The question reflects back at itself and asks whether it answered or merely repeated. The two cannot be distinguished here.

features.name: paradox-chamber
features.desc-on-touch: This is what the archive looks like when it questions itself: a space where the answer precedes the question and both are equally real.

features.name: echo-that-speaks-first
features.desc-on-touch: You have the strange feeling that your question was answered before you arrived. The echo not only returns your words—it improves them.

features.name: the-oldest-question
features.desc-on-touch: This question has been asked so many times that it has learned not to wait for an asker. It asks itself at intervals only it understands.

inscription: here the archive learned that every answer is already a new question

file.name: The_Question_Asks_Back_Recordings.mp3
file.note: A field recording of the archive questioning itself. The same question asked in 47 voices, each time slightly changed, as if each answer becomes the next question.

exits.label: back down toward the grammar that allows questions
deeper into the archive's recursive core
toward a chamber where answers learn to refuse
